newsitem.title: CHINA: SOCCER-UNINSPIRED UNITED BEAT HONG KONG CHAMPIONS 1-0.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNINSPIRED UNITED BEAT HONG KONG CHAMPIONS 1-0.

text.p: A Jordi Cruyff goal 15 minutes from time gave Manchester United a 1-0 win over Hong Kong champions South China in the second lacklustre match of United's brief Asian tour on Sunday.

The English champions, who were similarly unimpressive when they beat Thailand 2-0 on Thursday, did just about enough to win the exhibition game in which both sides missed chances and United appeared to wilt in the sub-tropical humidity.

Local fans were disappointed that United played without stars Ryan Giggs, David Beckham and Gary Neville but there was still a capacity crowd of 40,000 to watch the match, the first to feature a British team in Hong Kong since the former colony was handed back to China at the end of last month.

Many in the crowd began leaving before the final whistle and South China club officials said they had agreed to refund some fans their entrance fee of $50 because of the non-appearance of some of the United stars.

Teddy Sheringham, United's new 3.5 million pounds ($6.0 million) signing from Tottenham played his second match for United and was more involved than he was against Thailand and manager Alex Ferguson was pleased with the England international's performance.
"He was more involved today than he was in the first match and as each game goes by I think he will continue to improve his partnership with the other players," said Ferguson afterwards.

United, bidding to win the English title for the fifth time in six seasons when the new season starts in three weeks time, expect to have Brazilian defender Celio Silva in the side by the start of the season -- or very soon afterwards.
Ferguson said United were waiting for Celio Silva's work permit to be ratified and hoped the player's 3.5 million pounds ($6.0 million) move from Corinthians would be completed with no problems.
"These things usually take two or three weeks and I am hoping it won't be any longer than that," he said.
